domain: Moral Philosophy / Historical Ethics / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of Spartan infant exposure practice as a test case for contested personhood boundaries across time. Examines whether the hillside-exposure reading represents a genuinely different moral constraint that has become unreachable from the modern ethical window, or whether it was always within the same possibility space but obscured by cultural drift.

key_entities: Spartan state (authority structure enforcing exposure practice)
Modern human rights framework (contemporary authority claiming universal personhood)
Apothetae (hillside exposure site; physical mechanism of exclusion)
key_tensions: State eugenic interest vs individual infant survival (Spartan practice vs modern rights)
Conditional personhood vs inherent personhood (exposure-permitting vs exposure-prohibiting readings)

mechanisms.description: Council inspection of newborns for fitness; authorization of exposure for those deemed unfit
Physical removal to hillside site; death by exposure as mechanism of population control

absences: No evidence of infant consent mechanisms (expected in modern framework, absent in Spartan)
No recorded Spartan ethical debate over exposure legitimacy (practice treated as uncontested)
No intermediate readings between full exposure permission and full prohibition (binary shift)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The personhood-boundary kernel: the point at which a human organism acquires moral standing sufficient to prohibit intentional killing
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: In Spartan context: state eugenic interest grounds interpretive authority. In modern context: inherent human dignity claims ground universal prohibition authority
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Petrification (Pattern 2) — revision of the personhood boundary is institutionally denied in both eras; drift accumulates as unreachable readings rather than acknowledged revision

readings.commitment: Moral standing contingent on state-assessed fitness; exposure of unfit infants is legitimate state action
readings.authority_grounding: State eugenic interest; collective survival priority over individual life
readings.expected_structural_delta: Infants judged unfit excluded from victim set; state authority to kill without murder classification; high suppression of parental autonomy

readings.commitment: Moral standing begins at live birth; all born infants possess equal standing regardless of fitness
readings.authority_grounding: Inherent human dignity; universal human rights framework
readings.expected_structural_delta: All born infants enter victim set; state killing classified as murder; parental protection duty rather than state inspection authority

readings.commitment: Moral standing begins at viability (capacity for independent survival); pre-viable organisms lack full standing
readings.authority_grounding: Biological capacity grounds moral status; medical determination of viability
readings.expected_structural_delta: Non-viable infants excluded from victim set; exposure of non-viable permitted; medical authority replaces state eugenic authority

omegas.description: Core analytical question: Did the conditional_fitness_reading DROP from the possibility space (became structurally impossible) or LEAVE the space (remains possible but institutionally suppressed)? If it dropped, what material constraint changed? If it left, what authority structure enforces the suppression?
omegas.source: Deferred axis path_naturalization_mechanism + kernel contest framing

omegas.description: Do the three readings emit genuinely different constraints or do they collapse under analysis? Viability_threshold_reading may collapse into conditional_fitness_reading if medical authority is functionally equivalent to state eugenic authority, or into birth_threshold_reading if viability determination is post-hoc rationalization of inherent dignity commitment.

Historical evidence for Spartan exposure practice comes primarily from Plutarch (writing 500+ years later) and may reflect Hellenistic projection rather than archaic Spartan reality. If practice is mythologized, the reading may never have been instantiated.
omegas.source: F34 (Epistemic Trespass) + extraction absence of contemporary Spartan sources

omegas.description: If conditional_fitness_reading remains structurally possible, what mechanism prevents its re-instantiation? Universal human rights declarations lack enforcement against state eugenic programs (see 20th century counterexamples). Is suppression institutional or merely rhetorical?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + commitment_system drift_status=absent
